relationships.subject: Delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol
relationships.evidence_quote: Δ9-THC mediates strongly state dependent inhibition of Cav3.2 channels with a preference for binding to inactivated channels

relationships.subject: Cav3.2
relationships.evidence_quote: As shown in Fig. 1h, Δ9-THC lost its analgesic effects when delivered to Cav3.2 null mice, indicating that the key biological target for spinally delivered Δ9-THC are T-type channels.

relationships.subject: Delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol
relationships.evidence_quote: Two days after CFA injection, intrathecal treatment with Δ9-THC (10 µg/i.t) but not with vehicle (10 µl/i.t.) resulted in anti-hyperalgesia that remained significant up to 3 h

key_findings: Intrathecal Δ9-THC produces analgesia in neuropathic, formalin and CFA pain models.
The analgesia is lost in Cav3.2 null mice but retained in CB1 and CB2 null mice, so spinal Δ9-THC acts via Cav3.2.
